summary_html: Cases arising on **federal lands/facilities** or involving **Indian children** invoke federal/tribal jurisdictional rules (VICAA for federal facilities; **ICWA** for Indian children and tribal preference/jurisdiction).
authority_html:
- **VICAA (34 U.S.C. §§ 20301–20307)** — federal-facility reporting mandates  
- **ICWA (25 U.S.C. §§ 1901–1963)** — tribal jurisdiction, placement preferences, notice to tribes

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Monroe County DHS v. Luis R.
key_cases.holding: ICWA sec. 1912(f) applies in a TPR even though the Indian child was already placed outside the parental home, and a county social worker without expertise beyond ordinary social-work qualifications is not a 'qualified expert witness'; sec. 1912(d) carries no beyond-a-reasonable-doubt burden.
key_cases.relevance: It is Wisconsin's leading published decision on how ICWA attaches once a case involves an Indian child.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that 25 U.S.C. § 1912 (f) applies even though the child has been placed outside the parental home before the TPR proceeding is filed.

key_cases.holding: In a TPR involving an Indian child the trial court correctly imposed a dual burden: proof beyond a reasonable doubt of ICWA's active-efforts and serious-damage elements, alongside the Children's Code elements.
key_cases.relevance: It establishes that ICWA supersedes the Children's Code in any covered custody proceeding in Wisconsin.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the trial court appropriately distributed the burden of proof according to the dictates of both the ICWA and the Wisconsin children's code.

key_cases.holding: Before denying a parent's ICWA request to transfer a case to tribal court, the circuit court must first ascertain whether the tribal court will accept jurisdiction and then decide whether good cause exists to deny transfer.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Wisconsin procedure for an ICWA transfer-to-tribal-court request.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that reversal is appropriate and, on remand, direct the circuit court to first ascertain whether the tribal court will accept jurisdiction.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: ICWA sec. 1912(f)'s heightened showing does not apply where the parent never had legal or physical custody of the Indian child, and sec. 1912(d)'s remedial-and-rehabilitative-efforts requirement applies only where terminating the parent's rights would precipitate the breakup of an Indian family.
key_cases.relevance: It limits when ICWA's heightened protections attach once a case involves an Indian child, and it postdates and narrows Wisconsin's Luis R. line.
key_cases.quote: we hold that §1912(d) applies only in cases where an Indian family's "breakup" would be precipitated by the termination of the parent's rights.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court rejected every challenge to the Indian Child Welfare Act - upholding Congress's Article I authority to enact it, rejecting the anticommandeering claims on the merits, and finding no standing for the equal protection and nondelegation claims - leaving ICWA's placement preferences and procedural requirements intact.
key_cases.relevance: It confirms that ICWA remains binding on Wisconsin counties and state courts, so the tribal-jurisdiction and notice machinery in the Wisconsin ICWA line is current law.
key_cases.quote: we reject all of petitioners' challenges to the statute, some on the merits and others for lack of standing.

state_agency.name: Wisconsin Department of Children and Families
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the county or tribal agency where the child lives — the list is at dcf.wisconsin.gov/reportabuse

mandatory_reporters: Physicians, naturopathic doctors, nurses, dentists, chiropractors, optometrists, acupuncturists, and medical or mental health professionals not otherwise specified (Wis. Stat. § 48.981(2)(a)1., 1m., 4.–9.)
Social workers, marriage and family therapists, and professional counselors (Wis. Stat. § 48.981(2)(a)10.–12.)
Public assistance workers, including financial and employment planners (Wis. Stat. § 48.981(2)(a)13.)
School teachers, school administrators, school counselors, and school employees not otherwise specified (Wis. Stat. § 48.981(2)(a)14.–16., 16m.)
Child care workers in a child care center, group home, or residential care center for children and youth, and child care providers (Wis. Stat. § 48.981(2)(a)18., 19.)
Alcohol or other drug abuse counselors and genetic counselors (Wis. Stat. § 48.981(2)(a)20., 20m.)

Treatment staff employed by or working under contract with a county department under Wis. Stat. § 46.23, 51.42, or 51.437, or with a residential care center for children and youth (Wis. Stat. § 48.981(2)(a)21.)
Physical therapists, physical therapist assistants, occupational therapists, and dietitians (Wis. Stat. § 48.981(2)(a)22., 22m., 23., 24.)
Emergency medical services practitioners and emergency medical responders (Wis. Stat. § 48.981(2)(a)27., 28.)
Police or law enforcement officers and juvenile correctional officers (Wis. Stat. § 48.981(2)(a)29., 30.)
Court-appointed special advocates, as to children seen in the course of activities under Wis. Stat. § 48.236(3) (Wis. Stat. § 48.981(2)(b))
Members of the clergy, except for child abuse information received solely through confidential communications made privately or in a confessional setting (Wis. Stat. § 48.981(2)(bm)1.–3.)
Any other person, including an attorney — permissive only; may report but is not required to (Wis. Stat. § 48.981(2)(c))

notice_requirements.timing: Within 24 hours after a county department that has a federally recognized reservation or the Ho-Chunk service area wholly or partly within its county receives a report about a child it knows or has reason to know is an Indian child residing in the county, or an Indian unborn child whose expectant mother resides in the county
content_required: Name and address of the Indian child or expectant mother
The fact that a report has been received about that Indian child or Indian unborn child

statutory_basis.citation_text: Wis. Stat. § 48.981(3)(bm) (notice of report to Indian tribal agent)
